sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that after respondent Nos.2 and 3 had filed applications under Section 28A of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 [for brevity, 'the L.A. Act'],
respondent No.1 has unnecessarily delayed disposal of the said applications, which has burdened the petitioner who is the beneficiary of the acquisition proceedings.
He submits that petitioner, who is the beneficiary, was not heard by respondent No.1 before passing the order impugned.

3. Per contra, learned counsel appearing for respondent Nos.2 and 3 submits that though notice was served on the petitioner, he had not appeared before the Land Acquisition Officer and therefore, it cannot be said that he was not heard in the matter.

He submits that under similar circumstances,
the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court in W.P.No.200652/2023 disposed of on 05.06.2024 has held that in the event the Reference Court has enhanced the compensation, the Land Acquisition Officer is duty bound to take steps to re-determine the NC: 2026:KHC-K:2076 HC-KAR compensation for all the land losers in respect of the acquisition proceedings which is under question and accordingly has dismissed the writ petition.

4. In the present case, the Reference Court in LAC Nos.256/2010, 257/2010 and 258/2010 has enhanced the compensation awarded to the land losers in respect of the lands which were subject matter of very same acquisition proceedings.

Subsequently, respondent Nos.2 to 4 also had filed application under Section 28A of the L.A. Act before respondent No.1 seeking enhanced compensation amount in terms of the order passed by the Reference Court in LAC Nos.256/2010,
257/2010 and 258/2010.

In identical circumstances, the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court in W.P.No.200652/2023 disposed of on 05.06.2024 in paragraph No.6 has observed as follows:
"6. It is not in dispute that the Reference Court in LAC No.470/2012, while considering a reference seeking higher compensation in respect of acquisition of a similarly situated land, enhanced the compensation determined by the Land Acquisition Officer.
Therefore, respondent No.1 was also entitled to be similarly treated by respondent No.2.

Therefore, no objections can be raised by the petitioner in the respondent No.1 making a claim for NC: 2026:KHC-K:2076 HC-KAR similar compensation paid to the land loser in LAC No.470/2012 by invoking Section 28(A)
of the L.A. Act.

As a matter of fact, having regard to the purport and purpose of Section 28(A) of the L.A. Act, it was incumbent upon respondent No.2 to have informed all the land losers in Hirapur village about the compensation enhanced by the Reference Court and he must have taken steps to re-determine the compensation for all the land losers in that village.
Since that was not done, respondent No.1 was justified in making a request to respondent No.2 to re-determine the compensation.

Therefore, the petitioner cannot challenge the award passed by respondent No.2,
re-determining the compensation."

sentences.text: It is not in dispute that the petitioner was issued with a notice by respondent No.1 in the proceedings that was initiated based on the application received by him from respondent Nos.2 to 4 under Section 28A of the L.A. Act.
Under the circumstances, I am of the opinion that no error apparent on the face of the record could be found in the order impugned which warrants interference by this Court.
If the petitioner is aggrieved by the delay in re-determining the compensation by respondent No.1, he is at liberty to proceed against respondent No.1 in accordance with law.
The petitioner shall pay the enhanced compensation amount to NC: 2026:KHC-K:2076 HC-KAR respondent Nos.2 to 4 within a period of two months from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
If any amount is deposited before this Court in this proceedings, the same shall be transferred to respondent No.1.
With the above observation, writ petition is disposed of.

Sd/-
